style_when: the story is a single number, rule, gate or shift and restraint is the point — with no scene to photograph, the frame must still be a real assembly: a modular bay, an unlatched inspection gate, a rack of blades, an interlocking connector
prompt: Minimalist modular mechanical assembly on a concrete substation plant floor: a heavy three-pole industrial circuit-breaker module with visibly open isolation jaws and a steel lockout hasp over the open handle, beside two identical matte black PLC control modules; both signal cables route to a single voltage tap on the still-live copper busbar above the open jaws, while the downstream busbar below is dark and disconnected. Hard raking key light from upper left across brushed steel and concrete, palette graphite, safety yellow, oxidised red, long cast contact shadows, generous negative space, extreme asymmetry with the breaker module left and the two PLC boxes right, no text, no logos.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, watermarks, illegible signage, captions, embossed or printed lettering
rationale: The story turns on a physical electrical configuration: an open breaker, an upstream voltage tap, and twin controllers reading the wrong node. A modular mechanical assembly can state the incorrect sensing topology with exact parts and restraint, avoiding a stock datacenter photo.
subject: An open industrial breaker module with two PLC control boxes wired to the live-side busbar above the open contacts.
core_thesis: A backup power system is only as independent as the evidence feeding it: when the generator start signal and the grid's post-event record are both read upstream of the device that isolates them, neither the site nor the utility can prove what happened.
core_conflict: A redundant 2N electrical path versus single-point voltage sensing upstream of the isolation breaker, so two controllers and the grid recorder share one blind observation.
composition: Extreme asymmetry, breaker module on the left third, two PLC boxes on the right, open contact gap at centre.

review.reason: The frame shows exactly the article's mechanism — an open breaker with its contacts exposed and two PLC controllers tapped off the live-side busbar — so a reader would recognise the story of a plant that cannot verify its own isolation.
